audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Pilate, Barabbas, crowd dynamics, mocking, crucifixion, Psalm lament, death, veil tearing, centurion confession, women witnesses, and Joseph burial.

verses.restored: Immediately in the morning, the chief priests with the elders, scribes, and whole council took counsel. Binding Jesus, they led him away and handed him over to Pilate.

familiar.text: And straightway in the morning the chief priests held a consultation with the elders and scribes and the whole council, and bound Jesus, and carried him away, and delivered him to Pilate.

modern.text: Early in the morning, the chief priests, elders, scribes, and the whole Sanhedrin devised a plan. They bound Jesus, led Him away, and handed Him over to Pilate.

original.text: Καὶ ⸀εὐθὺς πρωῒ συμβούλιον ποιήσαντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς μετὰ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ γραμματέων καὶ ὅλον τὸ συνέδριον δήσαντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπήνεγκαν καὶ ⸀παρέδωκαν Πιλάτῳ.

verses.restored: Pilate questioned him, Are you the king of the Judeans? He answered him, You say it.

familiar.text: And Pilate asked him, Art thou the King of the Jews? And he answering said unto him, Thou sayest it.

modern.text: So Pilate questioned Him, “Are You the King of the Jews?” “You have said so,” Jesus replied.

original.text: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων; ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς ⸂αὐτῷ λέγει⸃· Σὺ λέγεις.

verses.restored: The chief priests were accusing him of many things.

familiar.text: And the chief priests accused him of many things: but he answered nothing.

modern.text: And the chief priests began to accuse Him of many things.

original.text: καὶ κατηγόρουν αὐτοῦ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς πολλά.

verses.restored: Pilate again questioned him, saying, Do you answer nothing? See how many things they accuse you of.

familiar.text: And Pilate asked him again, saying, Answerest thou nothing? behold how many things they witness against thee.

modern.text: Then Pilate questioned Him again, “Have You no answer? Look how many charges they are bringing against You!”

original.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος πάλιν ⸀ἐπηρώτα αὐτὸν λέγων· Οὐκ ἀποκρίνῃ οὐδέν; ἴδε πόσα σου ⸀κατηγοροῦσιν.

verses.restored: But Jesus no longer answered anything, so that Pilate marveled.

familiar.text: But Jesus yet answered nothing; so that Pilate marvelled.

modern.text: But to Pilate’s amazement, Jesus made no further reply. The Crowd Chooses Barabbas (Matthew 27:15–23; Luke 23:13–25)

original.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς οὐκέτι οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίθη, ὥστε θαυμάζειν τὸν Πιλᾶτον.

verses.restored: At the feast he would release for them one prisoner whom they requested.

familiar.text: Now at that feast he released unto them one prisoner, whomsoever they desired.

modern.text: Now it was Pilate’s custom at the feast to release to the people a prisoner of their choosing.

original.text: Κατὰ δὲ ἑορτὴν ἀπέλυεν αὐτοῖς ἕνα δέσμιον ⸂ὃν παρῃτοῦντο⸃.

verses.restored: There was one called Barabbas, bound with the rebels who had committed murder in the uprising.

familiar.text: And there was one named Barabbas, which lay bound with them that had made insurrection with him, who had committed murder in the insurrection.

modern.text: And a man named Barabbas was imprisoned with the rebels who had committed murder during the insurrection.

original.text: ἦν δὲ ὁ λεγόμενος Βαραββᾶς μετὰ τῶν ⸀στασιαστῶν δεδεμένος οἵτινες ἐν τῇ στάσει φόνον πεποιήκεισαν.

verses.restored: The crowd came up and began to ask him to do as he usually did for them.

familiar.text: And the multitude crying aloud began to desire him to do as he had ever done unto them.

modern.text: So the crowd went up and began asking Pilate to keep his custom.

original.text: καὶ ⸀ἀναβὰς ὁ ὄχλος ἤρξατο αἰτεῖσθαι ⸀καθὼς ἐποίει αὐτοῖς.

verses.restored: Pilate answered them, saying, Do you want me to release for you the king of the Judeans?

familiar.text: But Pilate answered them, saying, Will ye that I release unto you the King of the Jews?

modern.text: “Do you want me to release to you the King of the Jews?” Pilate asked.

original.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς λέγων· Θέλετε ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν τὸν βασιλέα τῶν Ἰουδαίων;

verses.restored: For he knew that the chief priests had handed him over because of envy.

familiar.text: For he knew that the chief priests had delivered him for envy.

modern.text: For he knew it was out of envy that the chief priests had handed Jesus over.

original.text: ἐγίνωσκεν γὰρ ὅτι διὰ φθόνον παραδεδώκεισαν αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς.

verses.restored: But the chief priests stirred up the crowd so that he would release Barabbas for them instead.

familiar.text: But the chief priests moved the people, that he should rather release Barabbas unto them.

modern.text: But the chief priests stirred up the crowd to have him release Barabbas to them instead. Pilate Delivers Up Jesus (Matthew 27:24–26)

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς ἀνέσεισαν τὸν ὄχλον ἵνα μᾶλλον τὸν Βαραββᾶν ἀπολύσῃ αὐτοῖς.

verses.restored: Pilate again answered and said to them, What then do you want me to do with the one you call king of the Judeans?

familiar.text: And Pilate answered and said again unto them, What will ye then that I shall do unto him whom ye call the King of the Jews?

modern.text: So Pilate asked them again, “What then do you want me to do with the One you call the King of the Jews?”

original.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ⸂πάλιν ἀποκριθεὶς ἔλεγεν⸃ αὐτοῖς· Τί οὖν ⸀θέλετε ποιήσω ⸂ὃν λέγετε⸃ ⸀τὸν βασιλέα τῶν Ἰουδαίων;

verses.restored: They cried out again, Crucify him.

familiar.text: And they cried out again, Crucify him.

modern.text: And they shouted back, “Crucify Him!”

original.text: οἱ δὲ πάλιν ἔκραξαν· Σταύρωσον αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Pilate said to them, Why, what harm has he done? But they cried out even more, Crucify him.

familiar.text: Then Pilate said unto them, Why, what evil hath he done? And they cried out the more exceedingly, Crucify him.

modern.text: “Why?” asked Pilate. “What evil has He done?” But they shouted all the louder, “Crucify Him!”

original.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Τί γὰρ ⸂ἐποίησεν κακόν⸃; οἱ δὲ ⸀περισσῶς ἔκραξαν· Σταύρωσον αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Pilate, wishing to satisfy the crowd, released Barabbas for them; and after flogging Jesus, he handed him over to be crucified.

familiar.text: And so Pilate, willing to content the people, released Barabbas unto them, and delivered Jesus, when he had scourged him, to be crucified.

modern.text: And wishing to satisfy the crowd, Pilate released Barabbas to them. But he had Jesus flogged, and handed Him over to be crucified. The Soldiers Mock Jesus (Isaiah 50:4–11; Matthew 27:27–31; Luke 22:63–65; John 19:1–15)

original.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος βουλόμενος τῷ ὄχλῳ τὸ ἱκανὸν ποιῆσαι ἀπέλυσεν αὐτοῖς τὸν Βαραββᾶν, καὶ παρέδωκεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν φραγελλώσας ἵνα σταυρωθῇ.

verses.restored: The soldiers led him away inside the courtyard, that is, the praetorium, and called together the whole cohort.

familiar.text: And the soldiers led him away into the hall, called Praetorium; and they call together the whole band.

modern.text: Then the soldiers led Jesus away into the palace (that is, the Praetorium) and called the whole company together.

original.text: Οἱ δὲ στρατιῶται ἀπήγαγον αὐτὸν ἔσω τῆς αὐλῆς, ὅ ἐστιν πραιτώριον, καὶ συγκαλοῦσιν ὅλην τὴν σπεῖραν.

verses.restored: They clothed him in purple, and twisting a thorn crown, they placed it on him.

familiar.text: And they clothed him with purple, and platted a crown of thorns, and put it about his head,

modern.text: They dressed Him in a purple robe, twisted together a crown of thorns, and set it on His head.

original.text: καὶ ⸀ἐνδιδύσκουσιν αὐτὸν πορφύραν καὶ περιτιθέασιν αὐτῷ πλέξαντες ἀκάνθινον στέφανον·

verses.restored: They began to greet him, Hail, king of the Judeans.

familiar.text: And began to salute him, Hail, King of the Jews!

modern.text: And they began to salute Him: “Hail, King of the Jews!”

original.text: καὶ ἤρξαντο ἀσπάζεσθαι αὐτόν· Χαῖρε, ⸀βασιλεῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων·

verses.restored: They struck his head with a reed, spat on him, and kneeling, bowed before him.

familiar.text: And they smote him on the head with a reed, and did spit upon him, and bowing their knees worshipped him.

modern.text: They kept striking His head with a staff and spitting on Him. And they knelt down and bowed before Him.

original.text: καὶ ἔτυπτον αὐτοῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν καλάμῳ καὶ ἐνέπτυον αὐτῷ, καὶ τιθέντες τὰ γόνατα προσεκύνουν αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: When they had mocked him, they stripped off the purple and put his own garments on him, and they led him out to crucify him.

familiar.text: And when they had mocked him, they took off the purple from him, and put his own clothes on him, and led him out to crucify him.

modern.text: After they had mocked Him, they removed the purple robe and put His own clothes back on Him. Then they led Him out to crucify Him. The Crucifixion (Psalms 22:1–31; Matthew 27:32–44; Luke 23:26–43; John 19:16–27)

original.text: καὶ ὅτε ἐνέπαιξαν αὐτῷ, ἐξέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὴν πορφύραν καὶ ἐνέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὰ ἱμάτια ⸂τὰ ἴδια⸃. καὶ ἐξάγουσιν αὐτὸν ἵνα ⸀σταυρώσωσιν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: They compel one passing by, Simon of Cyrene, coming from the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry his cross.

familiar.text: And they compel one Simon a Cyrenian, who passed by, coming out of the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to bear his cross.

modern.text: Now Simon of Cyrene, the father of Alexander and Rufus, was passing by on his way in from the country, and the soldiers forced him to carry the cross of Jesus.

original.text: Καὶ ἀγγαρεύουσιν παράγοντά τινα Σίμωνα Κυρηναῖον ἐρχόμενον ἀπʼ ἀγροῦ, τὸν πατέρα Ἀλεξάνδρου καὶ Ῥούφου, ἵνα ἄρῃ τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: They bring him to the place Golgotha, which is translated, Place of a Skull.

familiar.text: And they bring him unto the place Golgotha, which is, being interpreted, The place of a skull.

modern.text: They brought Jesus to a place called Golgotha, which means The Place of the Skull.

original.text: καὶ φέρουσιν αὐτὸν ἐπὶ ⸀τὸν ⸀Γολγοθᾶν τόπον, ὅ ἐστιν ⸀μεθερμηνευόμενον Κρανίου Τόπος.

verses.restored: They offered him wine mixed with myrrh, but he did not take it.

familiar.text: And they gave him to drink wine mingled with myrrh: but he received it not.

modern.text: There they offered Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He did not take it.

original.text: καὶ ἐδίδουν ⸀αὐτῷ ἐσμυρνισμένον οἶνον, ⸀ὃς δὲ οὐκ ἔλαβεν.

verses.restored: They crucify him and divide his garments, casting lots for them, who should take what.

familiar.text: And when they had crucified him, they parted his garments, casting lots upon them, what every man should take.

modern.text: And they crucified Him. They also divided His garments by casting lots to decide what each of them would take.

original.text: καὶ ⸂σταυροῦσιν αὐτὸν καὶ⸃ διαμερίζονται τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ, βάλλοντες κλῆρον ἐπʼ αὐτὰ τίς τί ἄρῃ.

verses.restored: It was the third hour, and they crucified him.

familiar.text: And it was the third hour, and they crucified him.

modern.text: It was the third hour when they crucified Him.

original.text: Ἦν δὲ ὥρα τρίτη καὶ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: The inscription of the charge against him was written: The King of the Judeans.

familiar.text: And the superscription of his accusation was written over, THE KING OF THE JEWS.

modern.text: And the charge inscribed against Him read: THE KING OF THE JEWS.

original.text: καὶ ἦν ἡ ἐπιγραφὴ τῆς αἰτίας αὐτοῦ ἐπιγεγραμμένη· Ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων.

verses.restored: With him they crucify two robbers, one at his right and one at his left.

familiar.text: And with him they crucify two thieves; the one on his right hand, and the other on his left.

modern.text: Along with Jesus, they crucified two robbers, one on His right and one on His left.

original.text: καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ σταυροῦσιν δύο λῃστάς, ἕνα ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ ἕνα ἐξ εὐωνύμων ⸀αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: [Some later manuscripts add: And the Scripture was fulfilled that says, He was counted with lawless ones.]

familiar.text: And the scripture was fulfilled, which saith, And he was numbered with the transgressors.

modern.note: The BSB follows modern critical-text practice here and does not print this traditional verse number as a separate verse.

original.note: This traditional verse number is not present as a separate verse in the SBLGNT base text; preserve as a textual-witness issue.

verses.restored: Those passing by blasphemed him, shaking their heads and saying, Ha! You who destroy the temple and build it in three days,

familiar.text: And they that passed by railed on him, wagging their heads, and saying, Ah, thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days,

modern.text: And those who passed by heaped abuse on Him, shaking their heads and saying, “Aha! You who are going to destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days,

original.text: Καὶ οἱ παραπορευόμενοι ἐβλασφήμουν αὐτὸν κινοῦντες τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν καὶ λέγοντες· Οὐὰ ὁ καταλύων τὸν ναὸν καὶ ⸂οἰκοδομῶν ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις⸃,

verses.restored: save yourself by coming down from the cross.

familiar.text: Save thyself, and come down from the cross.

modern.text: come down from the cross and save Yourself!”

original.text: σῶσον σεαυτὸν ⸀καταβὰς ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ.

verses.restored: Likewise the chief priests with the scribes mocked among themselves, saying, He saved others; himself he cannot save.

familiar.text: Likewise also the chief priests mocking said among themselves with the scribes, He saved others; himself he cannot save.

modern.text: In the same way, the chief priests and scribes mocked Him among themselves, saying, “He saved others, but He cannot save Himself!

original.text: ὁμοίως καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἐμπαίζοντες πρὸς ἀλλήλους μετὰ τῶν γραμματέων ἔλεγον· Ἄλλους ἔσωσεν, ἑαυτὸν οὐ δύναται σῶσαι·

verses.restored: Let the Messiah, the king of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and trust. Those crucified with him also reproached him.

familiar.text: Let Christ the King of Israel descend now from the cross, that we may see and believe. And they that were crucified with him reviled him.

modern.text: Let the Christ, the King of Israel, come down now from the cross, so that we may see and believe!” And even those who were crucified with Him berated Him. The Death of Jesus (Psalms 22:1–31; Matthew 27:45–56; Luke 23:44–49; John 19:28–30)

original.text: ὁ χριστὸς ὁ ⸀βασιλεὺς Ἰσραὴλ καταβάτω νῦν ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ, ἵνα ἴδωμεν καὶ ⸀πιστεύσωμεν. καὶ οἱ συνεσταυρωμένοι ⸀σὺν αὐτῷ ὠνείδιζον αὐτόν.

verses.restored: When the sixth hour came, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.

familiar.text: And when the sixth hour was come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.

modern.text: From the sixth hour until the ninth hour darkness came over all the land.

original.text: ⸂Καὶ γενομένης⸃ ὥρας ἕκτης σκότος ἐγένετο ἐφʼ ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης.

verses.restored: At the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a great voice, Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani? which is translated, My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?

familiar.text: And at the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? which is, being interpreted, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?

modern.text: At the ninth hour, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, “Eloi, Eloi, lema sabachthani?” which means, “My God, My God, why have You forsaken Me?”

original.text: καὶ τῇ ⸂ἐνάτῃ ὥρᾳ⸃ ἐβόησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς φωνῇ ⸀μεγάλῃ· Ἐλωῒ ἐλωῒ ⸀λεμὰ σαβαχθάνι; ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Ὁ θεός μου ὁ θεός μου, εἰς τί ⸂ἐγκατέλιπές με⸃;

verses.restored: Some of those standing by heard and said, Look, he calls Elijah.

familiar.text: And some of them that stood by, when they heard it, said, Behold, he calleth Elias.

modern.text: When some of those standing nearby heard this, they said, “Behold, He is calling Elijah.”

original.text: καί τινες τῶν παρεστηκότων ἀκούσαντες ἔλεγον· ⸀Ἴδε Ἠλίαν φωνεῖ.

verses.restored: Someone ran, filled a sponge with sour wine, put it on a reed, and gave him drink, saying, Leave him; let us see whether Elijah comes to take him down.

familiar.text: And one ran and filled a spunge full of vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave him to drink, saying, Let alone; let us see whether Elias will come to take him down.

modern.text: And someone ran and filled a sponge with sour wine. He put it on a reed and held it up for Jesus to drink, saying, “Leave Him alone. Let us see if Elijah comes to take Him down.”

original.text: δραμὼν δέ ⸂τις καὶ⸃ γεμίσας σπόγγον ὄξους ⸀περιθεὶς καλάμῳ ἐπότιζεν αὐτόν, λέγων· Ἄφετε ἴδωμεν εἰ ἔρχεται Ἠλίας καθελεῖν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Jesus, releasing a great voice, breathed out.

familiar.text: And Jesus cried with a loud voice, and gave up the ghost.

modern.text: But Jesus let out a loud cry and breathed His last.

original.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀφεὶς φωνὴν μεγάλην ἐξέπνευσεν.

verses.restored: The veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.

familiar.text: And the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom.

modern.text: And the veil of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom.

original.text: καὶ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ ἐσχίσθη εἰς δύο ἀπʼ ἄνωθεν ἕως κάτω.

verses.restored: When the centurion standing opposite him saw that in this way he breathed out, he said, Truly this human was Son of the Divine.

familiar.text: And when the centurion, which stood over against him, saw that he so cried out, and gave up the ghost, he said, Truly this man was the Son of God.

modern.text: When the centurion standing there in front of Jesus saw how He had breathed His last, he said, “Truly this man was the Son of God!”

original.text: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ κεντυρίων ὁ παρεστηκὼς ἐξ ἐναντίας αὐτοῦ ὅτι ⸀οὕτως ἐξέπνευσεν εἶπεν· Ἀληθῶς ⸂οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος⸃ υἱὸς ⸂θεοῦ ἦν⸃.

verses.restored: There were also women watching from afar, among whom were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the Little and Joses, and Salome.

familiar.text: There were also women looking on afar off: among whom was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome;

modern.text: And there were also women watching from a distance. Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger and of Joses, and Salome.

original.text: Ἦσαν δὲ καὶ γυναῖκες ἀπὸ μακρόθεν θεωροῦσαι, ἐν ⸀αἷς καὶ ⸀Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ⸀ἡ Ἰακώβου τοῦ μικροῦ καὶ ⸀Ἰωσῆτος μήτηρ καὶ Σαλώμη,

verses.restored: When he was in Galilee, they followed him and served him, and many other women came up with him to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: (Who also, when he was in Galilee, followed him, and ministered unto him;) and many other women which came up with him unto Jerusalem.

modern.text: These women had followed Jesus and ministered to Him while He was in Galilee, and there were many other women who had come up to Jerusalem with Him. The Burial of Jesus (Isaiah 53:9–12; Matthew 27:57–61; Luke 23:50–56; John 19:38–42)

original.text: ⸀αἳ ὅτε ἦν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ ἠκολούθουν αὐτῷ καὶ διηκόνουν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἄλλαι πολλαὶ αἱ συναναβᾶσαι αὐτῷ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.

verses.restored: When evening had already come, since it was Preparation, that is, the day before Sabbath,

familiar.text: And now when the even was come, because it was the preparation, that is, the day before the sabbath,

modern.text: Now it was already evening. Since it was Preparation Day (that is, the day before the Sabbath),

original.text: Καὶ ἤδη ὀψίας γενομένης, ἐπεὶ ἦν παρασκευή, ὅ ἐστιν ⸀προσάββατον,

verses.restored: Joseph of Arimathea, a respected council member who himself was waiting for the reign of the Divine, came boldly to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.

familiar.text: Joseph of Arimathaea, an honourable counsellor, which also waited for the kingdom of God, came, and went in boldly unto Pilate, and craved the body of Jesus.

modern.text: Joseph of Arimathea, a prominent Council member who himself was waiting for the kingdom of God, boldly went to Pilate to ask for the body of Jesus.

original.text: ⸀ἐλθὼν Ἰωσὴφ ⸀ὁ ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας εὐσχήμων βουλευτής, ὃς καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν προσδεχόμενος τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, τολμήσας εἰσῆλθεν πρὸς ⸀τὸν Πιλᾶτον καὶ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.

verses.restored: Pilate marveled that he had already died; calling the centurion, he asked whether he had been dead for some time.

familiar.text: And Pilate marvelled if he were already dead: and calling unto him the centurion, he asked him whether he had been any while dead.

modern.text: Pilate was surprised to hear that Jesus was already dead, so he summoned the centurion to ask if this was so.

original.text: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἐθαύμασεν εἰ ἤδη τέθνηκεν, καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τὸν κεντυρίωνα ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν εἰ ⸀πάλαι ἀπέθανεν·

verses.restored: Learning from the centurion, he granted the corpse to Joseph.

familiar.text: And when he knew it of the centurion, he gave the body to Joseph.

modern.text: When Pilate had confirmed it with the centurion, he granted the body to Joseph.

original.text: καὶ γνοὺς ἀπὸ τοῦ κεντυρίωνος ἐδωρήσατο τὸ ⸀πτῶμα τῷ Ἰωσήφ.

verses.restored: Buying a linen cloth, he took him down, wrapped him in the linen cloth, and placed him in a tomb that had been cut from rock. He rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.

familiar.text: And he bought fine linen, and took him down, and wrapped him in the linen, and laid him in a sepulchre which was hewn out of a rock, and rolled a stone unto the door of the sepulchre.

modern.text: So Joseph bought a linen cloth, took down the body of Jesus, wrapped it in the cloth, and placed it in a tomb that had been cut out of the rock. Then he rolled a stone against the entrance to the tomb.

original.text: καὶ ἀγοράσας ⸀σινδόνα καθελὼν αὐτὸν ἐνείλησεν τῇ σινδόνι καὶ ⸀ἔθηκεν αὐτὸν ἐν ⸀μνημείῳ ὃ ἦν λελατομημένον ἐκ πέτρας, καὶ προσεκύλισεν λίθον ἐπὶ τὴν θύραν τοῦ μνημείου.

verses.restored: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses were watching where he was placed.
